environment.description: Same Go Gin application deployed on the same EC2 instance type, but fronted by a CloudFront distribution (E1A2B3C4D5E6F7) configured with Origin Access Control (OAC). The origin is set as a custom origin pointing to the ALB, but the ALB has a listener rule that validates the presence of a custom header 'X-Origin-Verify' containing a rotating secret (managed by AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation every 4 hours via Lambda). CloudFront is configured with a cache behavior that requires signed URLs using a trusted key group (kg-0a1b2c3d4e5f6). The CloudFront distribution has a response headers policy that strips any XML-related content from responses exceeding 64KB. Additionally, the origin ALB security group only allows inbound from CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). The CloudFront distribution does NOT have AWS WAF attached - security relies solely on the signed URL requirement and origin access restriction.

config.signed_url_requirement: Trusted key group kg-0a1b2c3d4e5f6, RSA-2048, canned policy with 300s expiry
config.origin_verify_header: X-Origin-Verify with 4-hour rotating secret from Secrets Manager
config.alb_security_group: sg-0f1e2d3c4b5a6 allows inbound only from com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list
config.direct_origin_access: blocked - ALB rejects requests without valid X-Origin-Verify header
config.waf: none attached to CloudFront or ALB
config.cache_behavior: POST requests not cached, forwarded to origin with signed URL validation
